text:
marie: Heads up — saw a latency spike on staging for v3 causal runs. Spike correlates with model builds that have head_dim=18. Graph: https://perf.redwood/staging/v3/ops/1743 (look at p50->p95 around Tue)
ajit: Rough numbers? p95 jump how big?
marie: p50 ~ 22ms -> 24ms, p95 68ms -> 210ms on some requests. Only for seq_len >= 384 and when using causal path.
dmitri: Ran the kernel profiler on a repro. Kernel chooser is flipping to the fallback SDPA slowpath (sdpa_baseline) when heads=18. Profiler snippet:
```
PROF: model=llama-v3-small head_dim=18 seq=512
  chosen_kernel: sdpa_baseline
  alternatives: flash_v3_causal (est_cost=120us), sdpa_baseline (est_cost=85us)
  measured: flash_v3_causal -> 320us (oom-tile fallback), sdpa_baseline -> 210us
  reason: tile alignment failure for flash_v3_causal with head chunking
```
marie: interesting that estimator picked sdpa but measured flash was worse due to tile fallback OOM.
sara: Two thoughts: (1) autotuner's probe matrix doesn't exercise the exact head grain for 18 (we probe multiples of 8/16). (2) the compile-time tiler expects head_dim % 8 == 0 for fast kernels. For odd multiples like 18 we hit a different codepath that can overflow shared mem and then fallback to a slower kernel.
ben: Quick mitigation: pad head_dim to 20 during kernel selection/compile (virtually, via padding at weight layout) so flash_v3 sees an aligned shape. Tradeoff: small extra memory for KV caches (20/18 ~= +11% keys). Also must ensure kv-cache indexing uses true length vs padded length.
ajit: Can you paste the probe change you propose? I want to see config.
sara: Proposed autotuner snippet:
```
# autotuner config
probe_granularity: [8, 4, 2]
pad_odd_heads: true
pad_threshold: 2  # only pad if pad <= pad_threshold
hysteresis_cycles: 2
warmup_probes: 3
```
sara: Explanation: add smaller granularity probes so we explicitly measure head_dim=18/22 etc, add optional padding up to 2 (so 18->20), and require 2 consecutive probes before flipping kernel choice to avoid flapping.
marie: Also watch KV cache: if we pad, we need to keep logical sequence length identical so prefix caching still hits. Ben, can you confirm padding doesn't shift kv indexing?
ben: Confirmed: we can apply padding in internal layout only; KV indices map to logical positions. Need to update the packed KV stride calculation and add a unit test for cache equivalence. I ran a microbench: padding 18->20 increased kv-mem by 11% and reduced median latency by ~35% on the repro.
dmitri: Another angle: add a compile-time try-schedule pass that rejects flash_v3 tiles that require >shared_mem and instead picks a narrower tile or sdpa-flash hybrid. That avoids runtime OOM fallback (which is expensive).
marie: Good. Which fix should we land first? padding + autotuner probe seems fast to roll.
ajit: Agreed. Plan: (1) Sara open PR for probe config + hysteresis, tests for head dims 14/18/22. (2) Ben open PR for lightweight internal padding with KV unit tests. (3) Dmitri investigate scheduler to avoid OOM tile choices for next milestone.
infra-bot: job perf-repro/1734567890-01 finished: baseline run -> increased p95 reproduced. repro artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/staging/1734567890/ (logs + flamegraphs).
marie: I'll pair with Sara on the autotuner tests tomorrow. @ajit can you prioritize a canary on dedicated for this change after merged? :thumbsup:
ajit: yes, will queue canary on dedicated after green CI.
ben: I'll add a small note in the console that models with padded heads may show +KV memory in the allocation planner.
marie: Awesome. Thanks all — this matches the regression timeline. I'll file a short incident note and link to the PRs in the thread.
